Score pooling ·

Provinces that sat the same exam can be compared on it

A 616 in 宁夏 looks like the 99.5th percentile against 宁夏's own 48,000 candidates and the 95.6th against the 525,000 who sat the same 全国甲 paper. The second number is the real one. This grid is the source table that decides which is used: a province that wrote any part of its own paper keeps a scale nobody else shares, and everyone who sat a whole national paper reads against one pooled distribution.

Undergraduate admission rows that find a score percentile
    Pick a cell Its paper, the provinces that sat it, and how many candidates the pooled score table covers.

    Each row is a province, each column a year. A colored band means the province sat a whole national paper and pools with everyone else in that band. Hatched cells have no verified shared full-paper assignment: they may use local subjects, or their historical assignment has not yet been recovered. Years are taken from the data, with no fixed start or end.

    The shared reference population collapses

    Candidates covered by each pool's score table, stacked by year. The drop after 2020 is the reform: as provinces move to 选考 they leave the national pools and take their candidates with them. Thin bars in 2024 and 2025 are partly missing tables rather than missing people — only a couple of provinces in those pools publish a distribution at all.

    Lineage

    全国I and 全国II merged into 全国乙 in 2021; 全国III was renamed 全国甲 the same year, so the teal band runs unbroken through the rename.

    Split by track, always

    文科 and 理科 sat different 数学 and different 综合, and 历史类 and 物理类 draw different people. A pool is a paper, a year, and a track — the three never mix.

    Wide bands read off narrow ones

    宁夏 publishes ten scores a row where 河南 publishes one. Rather than spreading a wide band evenly, each band splits by the per-score shape its own pool published, falling back to uniform only where the pool published nothing.

    Sources

    Assignments are hand-entered in province_year_paper.tsv with a citation per row, from 中国教育在线, 腾讯新闻 and 高考100.

    CoverageShareSeats

    Seats are weights, reported or estimated—not an extra quality category. A usable cutoff also covers the remaining seats of that school and exam track as a proxy; missing major detail is not missing intake. Major/group coverage means directly attached detail, while collapsed historical major summaries count as track proxies. Intake is estimated independently of cutoff availability: a fixed school mix from complete plan years, with a robust trend in seats per provincial age cohort. Missing schools or tracks stay in the denominator, including at either end of the time series. Arts/history and science/physics labels are bridged across reforms; their cutoffs are not. Named missing tracks are retained even below the old interpolation threshold (0%). Population projections use the official 2010 census age bands, interpolated without jumps between buckets. They are not exam registrations and do not measure subsequent migration. Select a province to compare the estimate with raw plans and seats attached to cutoff rows. Historical school mixes and long-range seat-rate trends remain estimates, not exact intake counts. Vocational admissions are excluded from both views.

    Score distributions

    Where each table stops carrying candidates

    Candidates at or above a score, log scale, one curve per province. Thick curves are pools; thin ones are their members. A curve that ends mid-air is a table that stops there, and below that point the pool counts everyone except that province.

    Weight a pool by its members' floors. A member whose table stops at 400 contributes nothing below it, so the pooled counts there are short by that province and every percentile drawn from them reads high.

    PaperProvince Floor scoreCounted there Scores below the pool's floor

    A member's floor against the deepest floor in its pool. The gap is the stretch of scores the pool prices without that province.

    Seats

    Every school takes more students at home. Some provinces never say so.

    A school's home seats as a share of its estimated national total, against its home province's share of the country's candidates. Home bias is real and large, so a school sitting near the diagonal published no count where it sits.

    浙江 publishes six bars for 浙江大学 and no count against any of them, so its home seats read 79 a year against a real intake near 3,000.

    Home bias falls as a school gets abler

    Each dot is a school priced across at least half its provinces: its intake's median percentile against how many times its home province's candidate share it takes at home. The line joins the median of each ability fifth. The weakest fifth takes home fifteen times over; the ablest, eight. A national university recruits nationally, and the rest are local institutions that award a national degree.

    More students, or an easier bar? They are different questions

    Taking more students at home explains itself: candidates apply near home. It says nothing about the line they had to clear. Below, each dot is a school with both measured — how many times its province's share it takes at home, against how much further down the national ranking its home admits sit than its away admits.

    Above the dashed line a school's home admits stand lower than its away admits. Two thirds of schools sit there, and the median takes home a fifth further from the top. But the two biases barely move together — a school can take most of its class locally and hold one line, or hold few seats at home and drop the line sharply for them.

    Abler schools open the home door wider

    The two measures disagree, and the disagreement is the point. Counted as candidates in a hundred, the weakest schools discount most — eleven in a hundred sit between their two bars against three at the top. Counted as how many times more of the province clears the home bar, it reverses: the ablest fifth opens its home door 1.6 times wider, the middle barely at all. A weak school admits from most of its province either way, so ten points there changes little; four points at 复旦大学 is the difference between the top 0.15 percent and the top 4.5 percent.

    What the pooling lets us ask

    Same paper, different provinces

    A score means nothing across provinces that sat different exams, which is why everything above works in percentiles. Where provinces shared a paper the scores are the same measurement, and the comparison the percentile machinery exists to avoid becomes the one worth making.

    Keep every published band. Where a table stops early, estimate the missing lower part using a better-covered year's shape and a candidate total borrowed from neighbouring years or cohort counts. A thin table contributes less information, not a higher floor for everyone.

    Points are observed or reconstructed means; grey bars show one within-province standard deviation either side, not confidence intervals. Smaller, fainter points carry less information. Hover for the original mean, published and estimated candidate counts, model error and fractional weight. These are exam candidates, not the entire age cohort.

    All of them at once, linked through the papers they share

    No paper is sat by everybody, so no single comparison ranks the country. They overlap, though: 河南 sits with 河北 one year and 山西 another, 山西 sits with 甘肃, and the chain reaches most of the country. A province's mean on a paper is read as its own standing plus that paper's difficulty, and both are solved for together — which is what stops the obvious method being slightly wrong. Measuring each province against the average of whoever it happened to sit beside makes the baseline depend on the company, so a province that mostly sits with strong neighbours is marked down for their company rather than its own candidates. Each table's contribution is weighted by its reconstruction error and uncertainty in the candidate total, rather than by the number of people in the province.

    The bar behind each point is one standard deviation of that province's own candidates, so the gaps between provinces can be read against the gaps between students. These spreads also include the modelled lower tail where necessary. Zero is the equal-weight mean of the fitted province effects, not a population-weighted mean. Hover for raw versus effective paper counts and the range of individual-paper estimates.

    One complete table contributes at most one unit of information. Extra error reduces that weight continuously; no shared-paper table is dropped for a high cutoff or small candidate count. Disconnected paper networks have separate origins and are never ranked against each other.

    Which door, which student

    Every route into 北大 and 清华, on one axis

    Percentiles this high differ only in how small 100 − p is, so the axis is that tail on a log scale. A curve further right admits candidates further from the top of the country.

    强基计划 never reaches a provincial file, so its curve comes from the pool its entry lines imply. It is the only route here whose shape is inferred rather than measured.

    The route that bypasses the batches admits below the one that does not, at both schools. That is what a separate door is for, and it is invisible to anyone reading only the published cutoffs.

    Every curve is one year's seats: measured seats divided by the years they cover, then raised by the share of candidates the provinces they appear in hold. 北京大学's own figure for 普通批 and 提前批 together in 2024 is 1,886, against the 1,968 these two curves carry, and its 强基计划 is about 900 against the 904 drawn here. Use the second view to compare shapes once a small route flattens against a large one.

    Who may skip the exam

    The master's exam got harder. The other door never opened.

    Registrations for the December exam rose from 1.5 to 4.7 million while places rose far more slowly. The headline odds still understate it, because a growing share of places never reaches the exam: they go by recommendation, and only listed schools may recommend.

    Candidates for each master's place

    Which schools may recommend at all

    Each band is five percentiles of undergraduate intake ability. Not one school below the fiftieth may recommend. The route is shut before a candidate sits anything, and what shuts it is which university took them at eighteen.
